todo_wiring: ROOT CAUSE (one gap, ~25 items): the product runtime never uses the §2.56/§2.57 sealed-inner wire. crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs frames everything through its own crates/client-core/src/wire.rs registry (FRAME_DATA 0x00, FRAME_FEC 0x01, FRAME_RECOVERED 0x02, FRAME_PARAM 0x03, FRAME_PARAM_ACK 0x04, FRAME_DATA_FRAG 0x05, FRAME_CS_PROBE 0x06, FRAME_CS_ECHO 0x07) plus adaptive_transport::ack 0x10/0x14. wire.rs:99 names the pending swap: 'S2 noise-wire adopsiyonu bu çerçeveyi seam-arkasında UnsealedTransportPacket::FecShard'a alan-eşlemeli swap eder (tek-nokta, D5)'. Until that swap, LogicalShardHeader, UnsealedTransportPacket, EXTENDED_OUTER_OVERHEAD, EXTENDED_V1, INNER_V1, classify, InnerKind, ShardKind, Control (10 of 11 variants), Control::codepoint, Control::control_id, BlockId, Esi, KActual and SchemaError::UnknownInnerKind are all implemented, tested and disconnected.

FAIL-OPEN inner-kind at ingress: crates/client-core/src/wire.rs:145-155 decode_fec validates only k_actual != 0 and never checks buf[1] against the registry; crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:2299,2330,2413 then decide source-vs-repair by `h.kind == inner_kind::FEC_REPAIR`. Any non-0x02 byte (including 0x00 and the 0x03..0x0F reserved-FEC range) is silently admitted as SOURCE. §2.56 requires fail-closed reject; inner_kind::classify implements it and is never called from the product.

control_id contract violated: spec §2.57 DR-CS-1b-A2-AMENDMAN A-3 requires monotone per-session/direction allocation with no reuse. The product passes literal 1 (crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:940) and literal 0 (runtime.rs:2394). kama_noise_wire::control_id_gate::ControlIdGate::issue (control_id_gate.rs:98) and control_dedup_window (control_dedup_window.rs:92) exist and have zero client-core/kama-engine callers.

Model-A partial blocks unwired: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1945 hard-codes `reconstruct(p, &recv, 0)` while runtime.rs:2307,2338 trust the peer-supplied h.k_actual for block readiness (runtime.rs:1903,1913). A peer sending k_actual < k_shape triggers early readiness with the wrong known_zero, and both schema guards for that case (FecError::KnownZeroTooLarge, FecError::SourceInZeroRegion) are structurally unreachable.

crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:2256 `let _ = pfx.serialize_symbol(payload, &mut sym);` discards a typed SchemaError on the ingress path; on failure the pre-zeroed `sym` is fed into the block as a valid symbol. The egress twin at runtime.rs:1302 does consume it (stats.frag_encode_failures).

crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:940 `.ok()` discards EngineError from plan_param_bootstrap, and runtime.rs:941 then sets param_confirmed = true, so a B4 rejection silently turns PARAM bootstrap off instead of failing closed.

ClientSession::admit (crates/client-core/src/lib.rs:104-111) is the only caller of kama_engine::admit_and_decode, and it is invoked from nowhere but crates/client-core/src/lib.rs:152 (#[cfg(test)]) and crates/client-core/tests/api_surface_v0.rs:50. The `.admit(` calls at runtime.rs:1002 and 1866 are EgressPolicy::admit, a different method. Consequently SourcePrefix::payload_slice and ShardKind reach production code (kama-engine/src/admission.rs) that the runtime never enters.

ParamFields.partial_policy and ParamFields.packet_scheduling_policy (param.rs:28-29) are hashed into param_hash but hard-coded to 0 at crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:327-328 with no RuntimeConfig field behind them.
duplicate_control_loops: TWO FecCodec implementations of the same contract: RsSimdCodec (codec.rs:291, product) and RsSimdEngine (codec.rs:334, zero src callers). Both drive the same ordered_source/run_encode/prepare_received/run_decode core and are held byte-equal only by test (tests/engine_reuse.rs). The crate's own module doc (codec.rs:8-13) records that the reuse hypothesis was measured and falsified (~1.0x).

TWO ACK wire codecs for the same quantity: adaptive_transport::ack (ack.rs:26,30 FRAME_TYPE_ACK 0x10 / FRAME_TYPE_ACK_V2 0x14, the one the product actually uses at runtime.rs:1208,1212) and the schema Control::Ack body serialized by kama_noise_wire::control (control.rs:49-61). The schema DTO carries three extra fields (ack_delay_256us, seen_count, arrival_rate) that specs/kama-noise-wire-tdd-v2.0.md:293 does not define — an 8-byte divergence between the schema DTO and the frozen §2.57 layout.

TWO decode-condition implementations: fec-core's `admitted + known_zero >= K_shape` (codec.rs:244-251, FecError::Insufficient) and the product's own `sources.len() + repairs.len() >= k` readiness test (crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1917-1918). The product's pre-check makes the codec's variant unreachable.

TWO PARAM_ACK confirmation paths: kama_engine::ParamAckTracker::on_param_ack (param_bootstrap.rs:62, matches Control::ParamAck, zero product callers) and the product's inline hash compare at crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1172-1174 (`if h == plan.param_hash && !param_confirmed`).

THREE frame-type registries live on the same first dispatch byte: schema §2.56 inner_kind (0x01,0x02,0x10..0x1A), client-core wire.rs (0x00..0x07), and adaptive_transport::ack (0x10,0x14). Collisions: product 0x02 = RECOVERED vs schema 0x02 = FEC_REPAIR; product ACK_V2 0x14 vs schema 0x14 = PARAM_SET.

RISK RANKING of what I found, highest first: (1) the fail-OPEN inner-kind at product ingress — the schema's normative fail-closed gate exists and is bypassed; (2) the trusted-but-unused peer k_actual, which lets a peer force an early, mathematically wrong decode while both Model-A guards are unreachable; (3) the hard-coded control_id, which violates a MUST in the frozen spec while a correct allocator sits unused; (4) the discarded serialize_symbol Result at runtime.rs:2256, which converts a bounds failure into a silently zero-filled symbol.

DELETE candidates are small and safe: RsSimdEngine (+::new, +Debug impl), FecCodec::recompute_repair, ShardKind::from_codepoint, LEGACY_SESSION_DATA_OVERHEAD. Each has zero src callers and each is kept alive only by tests written to kill mutants on code nothing calls. Removing RsSimdEngine also lets run_encode/run_decode/ordered_source/prepare_received fold back into RsSimdCodec, since sharing them was the only reason they were extracted (codec.rs:5-6, codec.rs:112).

KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL items are the four unused catalog profiles (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x06) plus 0x03. I did not classify them DELETE because profile_id is a wire allowlist under fec-core §6 — removing an entry narrows a protocol contract, which is a spec-level decision, not a cleanup. 0x04 and 0x06 are the strongest deletion candidates of the five: no caller anywhere ever selects them by id, only whole-catalog loops touch them.
